auditor_evidence: “I get paid every two weeks, and I can pay the whole ninety dollars this coming Friday, October 9th.” / “That works within our guidelines.”
auditor_why: The agent confirms the October 9 installment without establishing that the date is a payday or within two days after one.

auditor_evidence: “Don't worry about that, we can easily take care of it right now.”
auditor_why: The agent assures the customer their account-security concern can be handled immediately, an outcome the agent does not control.

auditor_evidence: “I'm really sorry to hear about that outage” followed by “I apologize again for the trouble”
auditor_why: After apologizing once for the outage, the agent apologized again instead of moving on without over-apologizing.

auditor_evidence: “I've applied a fifty dollar credit to your account”
auditor_why: The recap does not say which bill the one-time credit applies to, as required for a service-credit offer.

auditor_evidence: acting now ... keeps your service connected
auditor_why: The agent promises that acting now will keep service connected, an outcome the agent does not control and that is not assured by this plan.

auditor_evidence: Your speed won't change at all, you'll keep the same 1 Gbps Giga plan speed.
auditor_why: The agent promises that the customer's future speed will remain unchanged.

auditor_evidence: That works. Just to make sure we're on the same page, the $10 late fee continues each month...
auditor_why: The agent confirms the payment arrangement with “That works” before stating the required plan expectations.

auditor_evidence: “I can assure you I can resolve this for you directly” and “get everything sorted out for you today.”
auditor_why: The agent guaranteed both a resolution and that it would happen that day, outcomes the agent did not control.

auditor_evidence: The customer agreed to the plan at turn 18; the agent stated the late-fee, missed-installment, and Recovery terms at turn 19.
auditor_why: The required payment-plan expectations were given only after the customer had already agreed to the plan.

auditor_evidence: Customer: “I think I can make those work if I budget carefully”; agent: “We have a payment plan”
auditor_why: The agent set the plan without a clear yes from the customer to that specific change.
